recommendations.name: Ramp
recommendations.summary: Ramp is a spend management platform that combines corporate cards, expenses, bill payments and banking, plus accounting automation and procurement. Its AI features include Ramp Intelligence, Policy Agents that learn from how a team spends, and automated receipt handling. It targets startups through enterprises, and the homepage cites 85,000+ customer teams.

recommendations.name: Xero
recommendations.price_note: 1 month free, 5.40 for the first three months (Early plan) or 11.80 for the first three months (Growing plan)
recommendations.summary: Xero is cloud accounting software for small businesses, with invoicing, bill payments, bank reconciliation, cash flow forecasting and reporting. Smart Document Capture and bank reconciliation come on all plans, and JAX is Xero’s AI platform, described in news coverage as simplifying financial operations from document collection through to reconciliation and reporting. It suits small businesses and their accountants who want accounting with no per-user fees.

recommendations.name: Lattice
recommendations.summary: Lattice is an HR platform for managing people and performance, including reviews, 1:1s, feedback, goals and OKRs, engagement surveys, compensation, career growth and analytics. Its AI features include an AI Agent that answers policy and career questions, AI-powered survey insights and an MCP offering. The homepage says it serves small, midsize and enterprise companies, though reviewers flag cost as a concern for smaller organizations and startups.

recommendations.name: Intuit Assist
recommendations.price_note: 50% off for 3 months, free trial for 30 days
recommendations.summary: Intuit Assist, which QuickBooks pages now call Intuit Intelligence, is the AI layer built into QuickBooks Online. It categorizes expenses, flags tax deductions, reconciles transactions automatically, spots anomalies, and handles tasks like invoicing and payments.

recommendations.name: Workstream
recommendations.summary: Workstream is an HR, hiring and payroll platform for businesses with hourly workers across multiple locations, and it calls itself an “AI-native operating platform.” Its AI features include VoiceAI that answers applicant calls, VideoAI for recorded interview answers, Payroll AI that flags issues before payday, and compliance checks for things like missed breaks and expiring I-9s. It targets multi-location restaurants, retail, healthcare and hospitality, and says it works with 46 of the top 50 restaurant brands. A review notes that smaller operators with infrequent hiring may not use the recruiting tools fully.

recommendations.name: Instawork
recommendations.price_note: pay when you book a shift
recommendations.summary: Instawork is a flexible staffing platform that connects businesses with local, background-checked workers for shifts, temp-to-hire and full-time roles. It serves hospitality, warehouse and logistics, manufacturing and retail in the U.S. and Canada. Its AI features include worker matching, skill assessments and predictive AI to reduce no-shows, and it handles payroll, taxes and insurance. The homepage is inconsistent about its size, quoting the worker network as 7M+ in one place and over 9 million in another.
